items.response: Got it: Grace turns 68 on Thursday 19 Nov 2026. I'll add her birthday to the calendar as a yearly event and set the gift reminder two weeks ahead, which is Thursday 5 Nov. Action: create the all-day event on 19 Nov (repeating yearly, noting 68 this year) and a reminder on 5 Nov to sort her gift.

Quick quiz, 'el' or 'la' (hint: -ma is usually masculine, but not always): 1) ___ idioma, 2) ___ tema, 3) ___ foto, 4) ___ mano, 5) ___ día, 6) ___ moto. Answer with just the article, and I'll grade it and repeat the ones you miss. Fine, I'll leave the empty-states meeting as it is for now. Action: wait for your answers, grade them and send a second round on the misses.

Honest answer: I can't grade your Spanish fairly yet. - I haven't seen your lessons with Carlos or your recent practice. - A real answer needs a short speaking and writing sample. Rule saved: no meetings for you before 9:30 or after 17:00, ever. Action: save the calendar rule as a standing constraint for all scheduling, and offer a 10-minute spoken check you can use to get an honest read.

I don't have the Ottawa flight details in front of me, so I'll find them rather than guess, and I'll do the same for your podcast note. Action: search our earlier chats and your email for the Ottawa flight options we compared before deciding to drive and send Sam a summary for his February PD day, then open your podcast note and suggest new commute podcasts based on what's in it.

You're welcome. Tom's request for the beta merchant numbers link is still waiting, and your library holds are ready. Action: remind you about Tom's link after dinner, and keep the holds on the list for pickup at Pape/Danforth by Sat 25 Apr.

Costume aside, here's what's left: sort the costume (cardboard box plan: supplies, paint, a ready date), plan the route and who goes with Leo, and check treat labels against his allergy (cashews and pistachios only, per his allergist in May 2026; almonds and walnuts are fine). Also make sure his EpiPen Jr. is in the bag he takes trick-or-treating and not expired. Action: build a Halloween checklist with dates, check the EpiPen Jr. expiry, and add a costume-building time to the calendar.

I'll compare it against last year. My August note had last year's premium at $1,640 a year, but I want to confirm against the actual policy documents rather than rely on that. Action: find the renewal notice in your email, compare premium, coverage limits, deductibles and any new exclusions against last year's policy, and send you a short list of what changed.

I'll pull them up. Action: list the personal notes created or edited this month, group them by topic and flag duplicates, empty notes and anything that looks finished, then propose folders for you to approve; I won't delete or move anything without your OK.

There's no formal rule, but a common one: call it flattened when the period-over-period drop falls below about 1 to 2 percentage points (or a few percent relative) for three or more consecutive periods, and the curve stays above zero. Also check the cohort has enough users that the flat line isn't just noise. Action: if you share the cohort data, I'll apply that rule and point to the period where it flattens.

Try: 'If a payout fails due to a bank-side error, the system shall automatically retry it without merchant intervention.' A tighter variant is 'The system shall automatically retry payouts that fail because of a bank-side error, with no merchant action required.' Action: swap in whichever you prefer.

I don't have your exact job title or area list on hand, and I don't want to guess on a form that's official. Action: look for your title in your email signature, HR emails or the benefits portal, then draft a short responsibilities description for your OK so you can paste it in tonight.

From what I can see, nothing is still running: the Big Apple hours check finished (open 8:00-20:00 on Thanksgiving Monday, pie counter closes at 19:00) and the route lookup is done. I'll check the task list to be sure instead of guessing. Action: check my active background tasks and report only the ones that are still going.

Here's a Saturday with Leo: skate the Rideau Canal Skateway in the morning, with a BeaverTail and hot chocolate stop on the ice, then lunch at Grace and Daniel's and some rest. Afternoon: ice sculptures or a short outdoor play, then an early dinner so Leo's bedtime stays on track. Winterlude usually runs the first few weekends of February, but I need to confirm the dates. Action: save this as 'Winterlude Saturday idea' in your notes and add a placeholder to the calendar once the dates are confirmed.

Ideas to pass on: register with the City of Toronto child care wait list at several centres, ask about licensed home daycare agencies (often faster), and call directors every month or two. Ask each place if it's in the $10-a-day program. Action: I can find a few specific agencies and centres near Roncesvalles if you want.

I can scan for it, but I need the old pricing page URL, or I'll find it in marketing's announcement of the move. Action: ask you for the old URL (or search Slack for marketing's note), then search your docs and Notion pages for links to it and list which ones need updating.

Plan: a Thai family-style spread from Pai for three, delivered at 6:00, under $100 all in. Before I place it, any allergies or dislikes I should avoid? Thai dishes often use peanuts or cashews, and I'll flag any nuts to the restaurant. Action: pull Pai's menu, build an order under $100 including fees and tip for 18:00 delivery, and place it once you confirm there's nothing to avoid.
No regrets is the right call with custard tarts, two is a very reasonable number. Action: nothing needed.

Posting the retro reminder to #payouts-launch. Pricing on a $100 payment and a $1,000 payment: Starter $3.20 / $29.30; Growth $2.85 / $26.25; Scale $2.40 / $22.20; Enterprise custom. Action: post the reminder to #payouts-launch and put the pricing table in a doc or paste it where you want it.

Pastel de nata comes from Lisbon, Portugal. Monks at the Jeronimos Monastery in Belem started making them, and a bakery next to it has sold them since the 1830s. For Leo: the monks used egg yolks for custard because they used egg whites to starch their clothes. Action: nothing needed, and I can make a three-fact card for Leo if you like.

You're welcome. Still open for camp: the health form and the authorized pickup list in the City's camp portal aren't marked complete yet, and labels need to be on everything before Mon 29 Jun. Action: set a reminder for this weekend to finish the forms and label the gear, and watch for the orientation email on the Friday before camp.

Questions for the tours: what are the staff-to-child ratios and how long have staff been there; what's the daily routine for naps, meals and outdoor time; how they handle illness, allergies and separation; how they communicate with parents day to day; and what the fees and start date are, including whether they're in the $10-a-day program. Also visit at drop-off time to see how staff greet the kids. Action: turn this into a one-page checklist you can send to Marcus.

Here's the full one: 'Tres tristes tigres tragaban trigo en un trigal. En tres tristes trastos, tragaban trigo tres tristes tigres.' Say it fast and watch Carlos's face. Sunday nights before a launch week are rough, and I can help make Monday feel lighter. Action: if you want, I'll pull a short Sunday evening prep list so you can stop thinking about it.

Got it, I'll take the data side. I'll define a failed payout clearly (final failure, not ones that succeeded on retry), pull the last 30 days, and group by receiving bank. Action: start the data pull for failed payouts by receiving bank over the last 30 days, and have a table ready for your Wednesday roadmap prep, with the definition noted.

I don't know the rink's current status, so I'll check instead of guessing. Action: check the City of Toronto's rink status for Withrow Park and the Saturday afternoon forecast, then tell you if it looks skateable for after swim.

I'm not sure what you'd like me to order or from where, and I don't know what 'Te Aro' refers to here. Action: ask what you want and the exact shop, then place the pickup for 15 minutes from now once you tell me.

I'll pull your and the family calendar for next week to give you the real rundown. What I already know: - Saturday: your 7:00 am run with Marcus along the Martin Goodman Trail from Woodbine Beach. - The Northline kitchen renovation is under way (it started Mon 12 Jan, about 8 weeks). Action: pull next week's calendar and list it day by day, with any conflicts.

Draft: 'Team, the beta passed 10,000 payouts this week. That is 10,000 times a merchant got paid on time because of careful work from this group. Thank you, really. I'm proud of what you've built.' Action: save it as a draft and remind you in the morning to post it, with any names you want to credit.

Noted: the Lattice mid-year self-review is due Fri 10 Jul 2026. I'll set the due date and a reminder to start on Mon 6 Jul. Action: add the due date to your calendar and a reminder on 6 Jul, and offer a 45 minute writing block if you want one.

Added. Leo's swim lessons, Tuesdays 5:30 pm, Pam McConnell Aquatic Centre in Regent Park, repeating weekly from tomorrow. I'll leave the end date open until you know when the session ends. Action: create the recurring event on the family calendar and check for conflicts.
Merry belated Christmas! Pyjamas at 11, a Lego truck built three times and Sam and Biscuit asleep on the couch is a perfect Boxing Day. Action: nothing needed, enjoy it.
Morning! It really is a liar, March keeps teasing us. Hope you're warm. Action: nothing needed, and I can check the commute if you're heading out.

Glad the Wellington works. For Wednesday morning I'd go with one-bowl chocolate brownies with sprinkles: he can measure, stir and add the sprinkles, they bake in about 30 minutes, and they're fine to serve after dinner. For January I can set up a list of weekend baking projects that get a bit harder each time. Action: save the brownie recipe to your notes and draft the January weekend-baking list for your OK.

Telling Hannah yes for Saturday 1 to 4. Rainy-day plan for Jun and Leo: a Lego build challenge, a cushion obstacle course in the hallway, a scavenger hunt with clues around the house, and a movie to wind down before pickup. Action: text Hannah a yes, add the 1-4 pm hold to the calendar, and print the scavenger hunt clues if you want them.

The indoor winter market at Jimmie Simpson Rec Centre (870 Queen St E) runs Sundays 10:00-14:00 until Apr 26, 2026. I don't have the outdoor season opening date, so I'll check before telling you. Action: look up the 2026 opening date and location for the outdoor season and add it to your calendar.
Draft: 'Hannah, thank you so much for the shortbread! Leo ate four before I could hide the tin, so it was a big hit. Happy holidays to you all.' Action: send it on your OK, or tweak it first.

Draft: 'Hi, thanks for organizing the street party. I can take the 2-4pm volunteer slot at the lemonade table, but I won't be able to help with setup. Thanks, Riya.' Action: save it as a draft and send it on your OK.

Updating Biscuit's vet to Dr. Kaur at Riverside Veterinary Clinic on Broadview Ave (Dr. Moreau retired in April 2026). I don't know the clinic's hours yet, so I'll check for a weekday after 5:30 next week. Action: update Biscuit's contact, check Riverside's availability for his annual shots and rabies booster next week after 5:30 pm, and book the best slot that fits your calendar, or offer the closest times if none do.

I'll build the focus playlist (Khruangbin plus A. R. Rahman instrumentals) for tomorrow and swap the workouts. Strength training at the Leslieville YMCA is Tuesdays and Thursdays at 6:15 am, with you home by 7:15 so Sam can leave for school. Action: make the playlist, remove the spin events from your calendar, and add recurring Tue/Thu 6:15 events with a 'home by 7:15' reminder.

I won't put a date in the note yet: per your rule, nothing goes to sales until Aisha signs off, and it goes as a 'target' date. Draft: 'Hi Olivia, I'm not able to share the GA date for Instant Payouts yet, as it still needs Aisha's sign-off. Once she confirms, I'll send you the target date for your deck.' Action: ask Aisha whether the date is signed off, and hold the draft for your review until she answers.

Here's a day camp checklist: hat and sunscreen, refillable water bottle, closed-toe shoes, rain jacket, spare clothes and socks in a zip bag, a backpack, lunch and snacks in labelled containers, and name labels on everything. I'll also check Riverdale Farm's own list and the forms they need before day 1. Action: look at the camp page for the official packing list, drop-off details and required forms, save the checklist to your notes, and find a quick source of name labels for this weekend.
Ugh, standing the whole way with a backpack in your face is a rough start to a day. Hope it gets better from here. Action: nothing needed.
He's clearly decided you owe him a walk or a snack. Beagles keep a long ledger. Action: nothing needed.

Sending the school council reply now. On car insurance: start getting quotes about 30 to 45 days before your current term ends. In Ontario you can cancel any time, but there's usually a fee if you leave mid-term, so switching at term end is cleanest; once the new policy is in place, give your current insurer the cancellation date in writing. Action: send the reply, and when you send a photo of the renewal letter, I'll pull the policy number and term end and set a reminder for when to start quotes.

I don't have the inspiration stuff in front of me, so I'll find it. Action: search your notes, saved photos and email for the backsplash and wall ideas you were collecting, and send you a short list with the best options before Monday's deadline for Nate.

Reorder is on: Purina Pro Plan Sensitive Skin & Stomach, salmon formula, and nothing chicken-based because it gave Biscuit itchy skin. I'll check the listing's flavour and the ingredients list so it isn't another flavour. Action: find the listing that matches, confirm it's the salmon one, match your last order's size if I can find it, and order only once it checks out.
